statements.quote: Medicare-for-all
statements.claim: Supports Medicare for All as part of the campaign's progressive legislative agenda.

statements.quote: 100 percent renewable energy by 2035
statements.claim: Supports a nationwide 100-percent renewable-energy target by2035 and a trillion-dollar clean-energy/infrastructure program.

statements.quote: leading with a bold progressive vision
statements.claim: Argues for building support around a progressive agenda rather than beginning negotiations in the middle; also describes accepting incremental gains without abandoning goals.

statements.quote: not accepting a dollar from corporations
statements.claim: States that the campaign rejects corporate and lobbyist money; not an independent finance audit.

statements.quote: Green New Deal
statements.claim: Presents large-scale public clean-energy and infrastructure investment as a jobs and climate program.

statements.quote: single-payer, universal health care system
statements.claim: Supports single-payer as a practical way to improve outcomes and reduce overall costs.

statements.quote: carbon taxes, national cap and trade markets
statements.claim: Proposes carbon pricing alongside renewable-energy deployment, infrastructure and recommitment to Paris.

statements.quote: focus on shared needs
statements.claim: Emphasizes coalition building and common needs rather than political talking points.

statements.quote: accelerate the deployment
statements.claim: Supports faster solar/wind deployment and resilient energy infrastructure.

statements.quote: expanding and increasing funding for Medicaid
statements.claim: Supports Medicaid and CHIP expansion, protecting Medicare and federal negotiation of prescription prices.

statements.quote: invest in sustainable sources and new technologies
statements.claim: Proposes federal investment in generation, storage and transmission of clean energy.

statements.quote: support increasing Social Security’s guaranteed benefits
statements.claim: Supports increased Social Security benefits rather than cuts.

statements.quote: demand a shift to renewable energy sources
statements.claim: Supports shifting from fossil fuels to renewables and reducing energy consumption.

statements.quote: focus more and more on results
statements.claim: Emphasizes prevention and results-oriented Medicare/Medicaid payment reform; this does not establish opposition to universal coverage.

statements.quote: controlling the prices for pharmaceuticals
statements.claim: Proposes federal action on drug prices and physician insurance costs.

statements.quote: take what works from each system
statements.claim: Would combine strengths of Medicare, Medicaid, ACA and VA coverage and fill gaps rather than start over.

statements.quote: develop a cohesive working relationship
statements.claim: Makes cooperation with Hawaii's delegation and allies across party lines his first priority.

statements.quote: Paris Climate Agreement
statements.claim: Supports returning to the Paris agreement and restoring environmental protections rolled back by Trump.

statements.quote: Medicare should be expanded to include all Americans
statements.claim: Supports Medicare access for everyone; the sentence alone does not specify every financing or private-insurance detail.

statements.quote: benefits should be increased and tied to inflation
statements.claim: Supports higher, inflation-linked Social Security benefits and increased contributions from high earners.

statements.quote: clean energy – wind, solar, geothermal
statements.claim: Supports switching to clean energy and following climate science.

statements.quote: find agreement both in your caucus and within the other party
statements.claim: Argues that debates must be followed by finding practical agreement within and across parties.

statements.quote: too much yelling and not enough talking
statements.claim: Presents dialogue and prior congressional experience as his approach. This is campaign rhetoric, not a measured effectiveness result.

comparisons.analysis: Both explicitly support a universal single-payer approach. Fukumoto frames it as fiscally practical; Ing places it in a progressive agenda. Their shared proposal is not erased by different rhetoric.
Ing names Medicare for All; Chin emphasizes expanding Medicaid/CHIP and protecting existing benefits. The selected Chin answer does not establish opposition to single-payer.
Ing proposes a universal insurance program; Kim emphasizes preventive care and results-oriented payment reforms. These address different dimensions and can coexist; no blanket opposition is inferred.
Ing champions Medicare for All, while Martin proposes combining and repairing existing systems. This records their stated reform approaches rather than assuming either rejects every other measure.
Both favor broad Medicare coverage. Ing names Medicare for All; Puletasi's sentence says Medicare should cover all Americans without supplying the full financing design.
Ing specifies a2035renewable endpoint; Fukumoto names carbon-pricing instruments and renewable deployment. A target and implementation tools are not opposing positions.

Ing emphasizes leading negotiations with a bold progressive vision; Fukumoto emphasizes shared needs and coalitions. Both describe willingness to work with others, so neither is labeled categorically unwilling to compromise.
Ing emphasizes agenda-setting around progressive policy; Martin emphasizes delegation cohesion and cross-party working relationships.
Ing argues for starting with a progressive vision; Case stresses finding agreement after debate. These are distinct stated approaches, not proof of complete ideological opposition.
